x: Second points were scored on our behalf by Abberton (Mile), Quackenbos (High Jump), Murdoch (880 yards), Sutton (Shot), and single points for third places came from Johns (220 yards and 100 yards), Lucas (Mile), Blyther (High Jump), Taylor (880 yards), F.
Tom Carter put up very good and plucky show and after Abberton, of Q.P.H.—he is also a member of the “Bels”—had led most of the way Tom looked like making up the lost ground with a lap to go.
Other successes were Carter, the mile, with Abberton 2nd. We also gained points in the field events.
Seven aside scored over a five-mile course; and Abberton showed the way home despite a very gallant effort on the part of Dobson, of the College.
In the 3 Miles the South were represented by Frank Abberton and Harry Shields, who has now taken over the track captain's job, as Frank Webb has been called up to the Forces.

Versus the Metropolitan Police A.C., at Hayes, on January 24th, over 5 miles. 1, Carter (26.40) ; 2, Peck (27.0) ; 4, Marchant ; 7, Shields ; 8, Clinton ; 9, Abberton ; 10, Mitchell ; 12, Johnson ; 16, Morrell.
Metcalfe, of the Poly, who are again assisting us this season. We had the individual winner of every track event and Frank Abberton, who was on leave, ran well to win the 2 Miles.

Dick Tobin lead the field out at a fair pace, then bunched together were Carter, Bill Lucas, Clinton, Abberton, Eales, Blowfield, Penny, with Footer and Morrell a little behind, and Len Herbert at the rear.
The positions of our members running for their counties was as follows: 10, D. Burfitt (M.), 49.20; 41, Abberton (S.), 51.1; 44, W.

Robertson, the Reading International runner, and with Bert Smith and Dick Tobin coming in behind one another in 7th and 8th places, we won the team race with individuals deleted by scoring 12 pts. to Portsmouth's 20 and T.V.H. 23. Abberton and McDonald ran as individuals and finished 6th and 10th respectively and A.
